Learn

In one line: one page for each technical topic that the team learned in a ticket, in plain language, with a link to the decision record or the PR.

Each page tells what the topic is, how it fits roomsie, the choice we made, and the gotchas. When a later ticket adds to a topic, the team updates its page. The list below is generated from the pages.

  • Alerts: email and browser push: a new request, an accept or a new message sends the other person an email and a browser push with no message text.
  • Areas, sub-areas and pockets: the areas table holds three levels (area groups, sub-areas and pockets), and a pick of an area includes each area under it.
  • Backups: each night, a GitHub workflow dumps the two databases, checks each restore, and keeps fourteen encrypted dumps in R2.
  • Building the API: tsx runs the TypeScript API in development, and tsup builds our code into one JavaScript file. The Docker image installs the libraries next to it.
  • The chat screen and the sign-in wall: /chat starts each goal. A guest types with no sign-in, and a tap that needs an account opens the sign-in wall.
  • CI checks: GitHub checks each pull request automatically, and main accepts a merge only when the checks pass and a teammate approves.
  • Deploys: Vercel publishes the web from main and builds a preview for each pull request. A GitHub workflow deploys the API as a Docker image to AWS Lightsail in Mumbai.
  • Form A and intent: Form A is the set of typed answers that drives matching, and intent is its first answer: the kind of place that a seeker wants.
  • ID checks and the Verified badge: a person sends an ID photo and a live selfie, a named reviewer decides, and roomsie keeps only the result.
  • The landing page: / is the public page that explains Roomsie. The server renders it, and moderators edit its quotes, links and details on admin pages with no code change.
  • Listings and photo uploads: a lister saves a listing of one of four kinds one step at a time, uploads photos straight to R2 with a signed link, and publishes it for 30 days.
  • Local development with Docker: a local Postgres 17 runs in Docker. pnpm db:up starts it, and pnpm test starts it if necessary and gives each test run a fresh database.
  • Message requests: "Say hi" sends a request with a short note, the other person accepts or declines, and only then can the two people chat; a phone number never shows in public or in a note.
  • Messages and realtime: an accepted message request is a conversation; the API saves each message and sends it live to the two people on their private Supabase Realtime channels.
  • Database migrations: a migration is a committed SQL file that changes the shape of the database. The deploy applies the new migrations and the catalogue seed before the new API starts.
  • Model hosting and where user text goes: each chat message goes to a model provider, and the provider decides where the text is stored and if it trains on it; roomsie sends user text to the DeepSeek API.
  • Moderation: reports, blocks and the admin screen: a user reports or blocks a person; reports can hide a card or a listing at once, and a moderator reviews each report on the admin screen and dismisses it, keeps the hide, or suspends the account.
  • OpenAPI from Zod: the API makes its OpenAPI document from the Zod schemas in packages/contract. The document is committed, and a test fails when it is out of date.
  • Place detail and listing reports: a signed-in user opens the full detail of a place, and can report it; a safety report, or reports from two people, hide the listing at once.
  • pnpm, Corepack and Turborepo: pnpm installs the packages of the monorepo, Corepack gives each developer the same pnpm version, and Turborepo runs the tasks of all packages with one command.
  • Postgres drivers: a driver is the library that connects the API to Postgres. We use postgres.js under Drizzle, with prepared statements off for the Supabase pooler.
  • Profiles and cards: a signed-in user makes one profile with a name, an age of 18 or more and a gender; the card goes live by itself when it is complete, and other users read it through the API.
  • Saved: a signed-in user saves a place or a person with the Save button, and sees them again under Saved, in the tabs Places and People.
  • Secret scanning: gitleaks finds a password or a key in the code before the secret goes into the shared git history. Run pnpm secrets before each pull request.
  • Sign-in and tokens: the web signs in with Google through Firebase. The API checks the ID token locally and loads the users row.
  • Uptime monitoring: HetrixTools calls the health check of the API each minute. When the API stops, it sends an alert to the Telegram group of the team.
  • The web UI base: the web app takes its colours, type and spacing from theme tokens of the design system, builds each screen from a small set of shared components, and calls the API through one helper that sends the sign-in token.
